digests.summary_md: Today’s capital markets batch is dominated by a sweeping pivot cycle, as firms abandon legacy models for AI infrastructure and concentrated crypto treasuries—often with contested credibility. HIVE, GREE, and MIGI are repositioning datacenter footprints toward AI compute, while BTBT and PURR accumulate single-token treasuries and NAKA restructured as a Bitcoin holding company. CANG’s abrupt mining ramp and near-total BTC liquidation captures the whiplash risk. Crypto mark-to-market losses recur at BTCS and others, while BTM’s Chapter 11 filing marks a definitive endpoint. A counter-trend appears in ATCH, which shows genuine commercial traction after a balance-sheet clean-up. Across the batch, dilution from frequent share registrations, short-interest surges, and Nasdaq compliance battles (IPST, MIGI) reinforce fragile sentiment, leaving most narratives heavily dependent on management’s ability to convince markets that these transformations are more than opportunistic repositioning.
